note: What has changed about one unit. A flag byte says which groups of values follow, and each group that follows says which of its values it holds and carries them as a run of bytes. The groups follow in a fixed order that is not the order of the flags: the last flag's values come before the one before it, and the rest run in flag order. spec/replication.md says what settles the reading of a run, and records what a champion's groups carry.

bits.name: group4
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow. They come after every other group's, whatever the flags. Nothing observed has set this, so no layout is recorded for it. A reading end that meets it cannot tell where this unit's values end, so it cannot read the units after it in the same batch either.

bits.name: group5
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow. They come before the group numbered after it, not after.

fields.name: unit

fields.name: group0
fields.note: The values of group 0, where the flag says they follow.

fields.name: which
fields.note: Says which of the group's values the run below holds, one bit each, lowest first.

fields.name: length
fields.note: How many bytes the run below holds.

fields.name: values
fields.note: The values themselves, one after another in the order the bits above name them, lowest first. What each one is, and which of the two shapes it takes, is settled by the kind of unit rather than by anything here. spec/replication.md says so, and records what a champion's groups carry.
